raw_response:
I will not spread my 8.5 mu evenly. I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize, because that is the steady food-and-cash road here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton because cotton needs more looking after and my family has people working outside. I do not like gambling with yield. If I am unsure, I will follow what worked on my land and what the better growers around me did last year. On the wheat-maize land, I will feed wheat a bit heavier because wheat shows fast if fertilizer is short, then after wheat harvest I will put maize straight in quickly so I do not lose moisture or season. I have well water, so I will use it when the crop really needs it instead of waiting for the sky. Cotton I will keep on fewer mu, use decent seed, give it enough potash, and spray more times because once insects get ahead, cotton turns into trouble. I will spend money first where yield is safest, so wheat and maize get the main share, and cotton stays smaller.
